what_its_for: Mirabegron is used to treat overactive bladder (OAB). It helps reduce the sudden, strong urges to urinate, helps you urinate less often, and reduces accidental leaks of urine. It works by relaxing the bladder muscle so your bladder can hold more urine.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with a glass of water. Do NOT crush, chew, or cut the tablet in half, as this can release too much medicine at once. You can take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 25 mg once a day. Your doctor may increase your dose to 50 mg once a day after 8 weeks if needed. Always follow your doctor's instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time. Do NOT take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store mirabegron at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking other medications that can interact with mirabegron without checking with your pharmacist or doctor first, especially blood thinners like warfarin, certain heart rhythm medications, or other bladder medications. Let your doctor know about ALL medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take. Avoid activities that require alertness until you know how this medicine affects you.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: difficulty urinating or cannot urinate at all, a fast or irregular heartbeat, severe rash, hives, or swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat (signs of a serious allergic reaction), unusual increase in blood pressure, eye pain or vision changes, or signs of a urinary tract infection such as burning, pain, or fever.
when_it_works: Mirabegron may start to improve your symptoms within 4 to 8 weeks of starting treatment. You may notice fewer urgent trips to the bathroom and fewer accidents. Give the medication time to work fully before deciding if it is helping you.
special_populations: Older adults (65+): No dose adjustment is usually needed, but older patients may be more sensitive to side effects, especially high blood pressure. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may prescribe a lower dose if you have moderate to severe kidney or liver disease. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: It is not known if mirabegron is safe during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before taking this medication. Children: Mirabegron is not approved for use in children.
